diagnostic.summary: On TRAIN, btc-trend-24-72-demo generates a gross_return of 7.602 across turnover of 752, but fees (4.402) and slippage (0.4402) reduce net_return to 2.760 (90% CI [-0.4083, 20.69]). Performance is concentrated in trend_regime=bull (mean_net_return 0.0001275, 90% CI [3.457e-05, 0.0002158], 269 trades), liquidity_regime=deep (7.771e-05, 90% CI [1.945e-05, 0.0001362], 145 trades), sentiment_regime=greed (6.813e-05, 90% CI [9.439e-06, 0.0001277], 162 trades), and vol_regime=low (5.310e-05, 90% CI [3.674e-06, 0.0001047], 178 trades). It struggles in trend_regime=sideways (mean_net_return -2.081e-05, 90% CI [-7.177e-05, 3.189e-05]) and shows weak, indistinguishable-from-zero net returns in thin liquidity, high volatility, fear sentiment, and bear markets (where n_trades=2).

hypotheses.statement: The strategy performs positively in trend_regime=bull with mean_net_return of 0.0001275 per decision interval across 269 trades (90% CI [3.457e-05, 0.0002158], total_cost 0.3014), whereas overall train gross_return of 7.602 is heavily reduced by fees of 4.402 and slippage of 0.4402 to a net_return of 2.760.
caveats: No multiple-comparison correction across 9 scanned regime buckets.
Unconditional always_on net return 90% CI [-0.4083, 20.69] spans zero despite positive point estimate of 2.760.
hypotheses.suggested_test: Evaluate out-of-sample mean_net_return in trend_regime=bull; falsified if the 90% bootstrap CI of mean_net_return includes zero or is negative on validation/test splits.

hypotheses.statement: The strategy works better in liquidity_regime=deep (mean_net_return 7.771e-05, 90% CI [1.945e-05, 0.0001362], n_trades=145, total_cost=0.341) than in liquidity_regime=thin, where evidence is weak and mean_net_return is near zero at 7.179e-06 with a 90% CI spanning zero ([-4.786e-05, 5.991e-05], n_trades=231, total_cost=0.4862).
caveats: No multiple-comparison correction across the 9 scanned regime buckets.
Higher trade count (231 vs 145) in thin liquidity drives higher total_cost (0.4862 vs 0.341).
hypotheses.suggested_test: Compare mean_net_return between liquidity_regime=deep and liquidity_regime=thin out-of-sample; falsified if liquidity_regime=deep 90% CI spans zero or underperforms liquidity_regime=thin.

hypotheses.statement: The strategy achieves positive net returns in sentiment_regime=greed (mean_net_return 6.813e-05, 90% CI [9.439e-06, 0.0001277], n_trades=162) and vol_regime=low (mean_net_return 5.310e-05, 90% CI [3.674e-06, 0.0001047], n_trades=178), whereas CIs span zero in sentiment_regime=fear ([-4.077e-05, 6.468e-05]) and vol_regime=high ([-3.500e-05, 9.172e-05]).
caveats: Sentiment regime may correlate with trend_regime=bull and vol_regime=low; interaction effects are not isolated.
hypotheses.suggested_test: Test out-of-sample mean_net_return in sentiment_regime=greed and vol_regime=low; falsified if either bucket's 90% CI spans zero or turns negative out-of-sample.

hypotheses.statement: The strategy fails to generate reliable net returns in trend_regime=sideways, showing a negative point estimate (mean_net_return -2.081e-05 across 105 trades, total_cost 0.1991), though evidence is weak because the 90% CI [-7.177e-05, 3.189e-05] spans zero.
caveats: The 90% CI in trend_regime=sideways spans zero, making the negative point estimate statistically weak.
hypotheses.suggested_test: Measure mean_net_return in trend_regime=sideways on out-of-sample data; falsified if the strategy achieves a statistically significant positive mean_net_return (90% CI > 0) in sideways markets.

rejected_explanations: Positive performance in trend_regime=bear (mean_net_return 2.069e-05): rejected because n_trades is only 2 (below the 20-trade threshold) and the 90% CI [-3.548e-05, 8.134e-05] spans zero, despite incurring 0.3267 in total_cost.

Outperformance in vol_regime=high (mean_net_return 3.179e-05, n_trades=198) or sentiment_regime=fear (mean_net_return 1.730e-05, n_trades=214): rejected as weak because their 90% CIs ([-3.500e-05, 9.172e-05] and [-4.077e-05, 6.468e-05]) span zero.
limitations: Validation and test splits are unavailable; all findings are restricted to the train split.
9 regime buckets were scanned simultaneously without multiple-comparison correction, increasing false-discovery risk.
Unconditional always_on train net_return is 2.760 (Sharpe 0.7630, max_drawdown 0.6547), but its 90% CI [-0.4083, 20.69] spans zero.
Only marginal single-feature regime buckets are available; joint multi-regime conditioning cannot be directly observed.

proposals.rationale: H3 shows positive mean_net_return in sentiment_regime=greed (6.813e-05) while fear spans zero ([-4.077e-05, 6.468e-05]). Gating to 0.0 when fear_greed <= 28 (0.33 quantile) cuts train turnover from 752 to 540, raises net_return from 2.760 to 3.009 (+0.2488), improves Sharpe from 0.7630 to 0.8701, and lowers max_drawdown from 0.6547 to 0.4520.
proposals.falsification_test: Reject on validation if net_return underperforms always_on (delta_net_return_vs_always_on <= 0), if Sharpe ratio does not improve over always_on, or if the 90% CI of mean_net_return when fear_greed > 28 spans zero or is negative.

proposals.rationale: Based on H3 (weak returns in sentiment_regime=fear), scaling allocation to 0.5 when fear_greed <= 28 preserves avg_holding_bars (63.47) while reducing turnover from 752 to 646. On train, net_return rises from 2.760 to 3.095 (+0.3352), Sharpe improves from 0.7630 to 0.8520, Sortino from 0.7004 to 0.7672, and max_drawdown drops from 0.6547 to 0.5426.
proposals.falsification_test: Reject on validation if delta_net_return_vs_always_on <= 0, if Sharpe or Sortino ratios fail to exceed always_on, or if max_drawdown exceeds always_on.

proposals.rationale: H1 and H4 show strong returns in trend_regime=bull (mean_net_return 0.0001275) and weak/negative returns in non-bull regimes. Scaling size to 0.5 when momentum_7d <= -0.02482 (0.33 quantile) maintains full size 82.99% of the time, lifting train net_return from 2.760 to 3.124 (+0.3637), Sharpe from 0.7630 to 0.8270, and reducing max_drawdown from 0.6547 to 0.6069.
proposals.falsification_test: Reject on validation if delta_net_return_vs_always_on <= 0, if Sharpe ratio is lower than always_on, or if higher turnover (885 vs 752 on train) erodes out-of-sample net returns.

overfit_risks: Many gate policies were attempted on train until the gate-test budget was exhausted. Across evaluated train gates, every 90% ci_delta spans zero, including this gate's train ci_delta of [-10.75, 4.739] (ev_test_gate_tr_f2ebe6b36c).

The apparent validation gain (+0.3205) comes from gating just 3.42% of validation exposure during a major sentiment_regime shift (greed rose from 49.48% to 89.63%, ev_strategy_hea_36802850f0) and increased validation turnover slightly from 250 to 254 (ev_arbiter_eval_c025d0b4bd), rather than cutting turnover as hypothesized on train (540 vs 752).
fragile_samples: Severe sentiment regime shift between train and validation (ev_strategy_hea_36802850f0: sentiment_regime_shares total_variation 0.4016, with fear dropping from 50.52% in train to 10.37% in validation) causes the gate to be almost always on in validation: allocation_mix is 1.0 for 96.58% of in-position decisions and 0.0 for only 3.42% (ev_arbiter_eval_c025d0b4bd, vs 30.38% gated in train). Evaluating a 0.33-quantile gate on a 3.42% validation tail is fragile and under-sampled.

observations: Validation point estimates are positive (delta_net_return_vs_always_on +0.3205, net_return 1.665 vs 1.344, Sharpe 1.846 vs 1.602, max_drawdown 0.2551 vs 0.2895 in ev_arbiter_eval_c025d0b4bd), though the 90% ci_delta [-0.02005, 0.8678] still spans zero and train Sortino actually decreased from 0.7004 to 0.6628 (ev_test_gate_tr_f2ebe6b36c).

limitations: 16 distinct agent gate specs attempted (16 agent train tests logged, refused ones included); 15 distinct policies evaluated in total. Multiple-comparison risk applies to train and validation results.
The critic can veto a proposal (part of the pre-registered rule); the critic sees validation results.

Bad luck vs broken: validation 14-day blocks of the unchanged strategy are compared with Lane A's train-only 14-day range, and exposure, turnover, costs, volatility and regime frequencies are compared train vs validation (pre-registered thresholds in health.py). Code computes it; only the critic sees it.

Walk-forward: every agent gate and competitor is also scored on Lane A's expanding train folds (same windows and 2-bar embargo as the LightGBM walk-forward). Thresholds come from quantiles of the whole train window, so the folds are a stability check across train sub-periods, not unseen data, and they do not change the pre-registered selection.
Regime effects are associations under lagged features, not causal.
Returns convention: compounded simple returns after costs everywhere (Lane A contract); deltas and CIs use the same convention.
The verdict only says whether an agent gate earned one sealed look; Lane A's arbiter makes the strategy decision.
LightGBM competitor: single seed (7); its result can vary with the seed. Calibrated on late train instead of validation (spec deviation, keeps validation out-of-sample).
news_sentiment coverage 0%: not allowed in gates; market-only gating.
No news source configured: no news context, no market-only vs market+news ablation.

context.summary: Across the 4 best and 4 worst train weeks (ev_sentiment_ep_d4e0482482), overall Fear & Greed levels and 7-day changes do not cleanly separate good and bad weeks, though sample size is small (4 weeks per side). Two of the 4 best weeks (best_week_1, best_week_4) co-occurred with a greed-to-fear flip in the prior 3 days versus a train base rate of 0.0956072351421189 (binomial_p_value = 0.0481037504017162), while 0 of 4 worst weeks had prior 3-day flips (binomial_p_value = 1). Both best and worst weeks occurred during elevated sentiment as well as fearful sentiment: 3 of 4 worst weeks started in extreme greed (87, 84, 91) and 1 in extreme fear (11), while best weeks started between 33 and 83 with prior 7-day changes ranging from -17 to +22 (vs. -20 to +21 for worst weeks).

findings.statement: 2 of the 4 best train weeks (best_week_1 and best_week_4) co-occurred with a greed-to-fear flip in the prior 3 days (72 bars), compared with the train base rate of 0.0956072351421189 (binomial_p_value = 0.0481037504017162). Only 1 of the 4 best weeks (best_week_1) co-occurred with a fear-to-greed flip in the prior 3 days versus a base rate of 0.0930013576840538 (binomial_p_value = 0.323252674893775).
caveats: Sample is small with only 4 weeks per side.
Co-occurrence in time only, not causation.

findings.statement: 0 of the 4 worst train weeks (worst_week_1, worst_week_2, worst_week_3, worst_week_4) co-occurred with either a fear-to-greed flip (train base rate 0.0930013576840538, binomial_p_value = 1) or a greed-to-fear flip (train base rate 0.0956072351421189, binomial_p_value = 1) in the prior 3 days.
caveats: Sample is small with only 4 weeks per side.
Co-occurrence in time only, not causation.

findings.statement: Starting Fear & Greed levels and in-week averages do not cleanly separate best and worst weeks compared with the train mean Fear & Greed of 42.7779111120808. Best weeks started at 42 (best_week_1), 57 (best_week_2), 83 (best_week_3), and 33 (best_week_4), with in-week means of 61.4166666666667, 69.5714285714286, 82.9047619047619, and 49.4226190476191. Worst weeks started in extreme greed (>75) in 3 of 4 cases—87 (worst_week_1), 84 (worst_week_2), and 91 (worst_week_3)—and in extreme fear (<25) at 11 in worst_week_4, with in-week means of 76.1428571428571, 55.9285714285714, 78.8988095238095, and 16.8571428571429.
caveats: Sample is small with only 4 weeks per side.
Co-occurrence in time only, not causation.

findings.statement: Prior 7-day Fear & Greed changes and extreme sentiment shares overlap across best and worst weeks rather than separating them.
